items.title: Greg Thomas interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 2014
items.q: Kenny G is not a jazz musician. I’m not saying Kenny G can’t play. Kenny G has a nice tone on the soprano sax...

ctx.x: You’re doing yourself a large disservice.

Absolutely. And a disservice to a public who may not know jazz history. And if you are either calling yourself a jazz musician or allowing yourself, because you are an instrumentalist say, to actually be called a jazz musician and you’re not that — Kenny G is not a jazz musician. I’m not saying Kenny G can’t play. Kenny G has a nice tone on the soprano sax, and I don’t mean to just — you know there’s a group of people who just knee jerk condemnation of certain people and Kenny G is one of them. But I’m using him…
Herb Alpert. When I was a kid he was, and in fact I read a fact recently that Kenny G surpassed Herb Alpert as the largest selling instrumentalist. But Herb Alpert, no one © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-
